title: The second half of my Theatre Is Life @Edinburgh Festival Fringe reco...
transcript: welcome to part two of Fringe recommendations these are all of the 4/5 star reviews of shows that I saw on the second half of my French trip starting with the four star shows you have what if they ate the baby which is one of Xhloe and Natasha's three shows that they brought to the Fringe this year what if they ate the baby is this absurdist story of these two housewives meeting for a meal that goes off the rails I have also seen their other two shows one of which is on this list but this one is a four star for me because it doesn't quite have the impactful ending that the other two shows have but I still really thoroughly enjoy it and if you've never seen a xhloe and Natasha show go see at least one of them next up is Anna Hale's Control Freak which is a one woman show told with music all about Anna Hale going to therapy for her social anxiety and fear of getting sick in public Anna Hale is a really great storyteller and while all of the songs didn't quite have the songwriting level that I wanted from them they were just so much fun to listen to and she does a great job of presenting them I also think one of the challenges of one person shows is having a compelling narrative and this one absolutely does also at four stars is consumed at traverse this is a story of four different generations of women joining to celebrate the great grandmother's 90th birthday and all of a sudden all of these secrets start to come out very much in the same vane of an appropriate or august oSage County but make it Irish Consumed also has some of the best design that you will see at fringe this house incredibly well done another one person show is Grooming My Ass which is this young woman's story of telling how she not only was groomed as a teenager but also found her trans identity the overall arc of the story didn't quite work for me but the performance and the direction absolutely made up for it that I have to give it four stars I wish this story itself had stuck a better landing but I was along for the ride from start to finish next up was the absolutely insane Footballers Wives which is a musical adaptation of the soap opera of the same name I thought Footballers Wives was a reality tv show and I could not have been any more wrong one of the best scores that I heard at the fringe and there is a studio cast album that you can listen to right now my biggest thing with Footballers Wives is that it tried to cram in too many storylines and definitely felt like it was an edited down version for fringe of a much longer musical that I would like to see but this was so much fun from start to finish that I have so glad I made space for it in my schedule another four star recommendation is flush which is a place set in a women's restroom in a bar we see all of these characters go in and out of the restroom throughout the night you have the group of teenagers who snuck in with fake IDS you have the group of women there for a Hen do you have uh a work company party that's a costume party that's also at this bar and all of these women interact with each other very similar to how women at interact with each other in any sort of bar there is an emotional change in the story about halfway through that didn't fully land for me but the concept and the way that it was performed was just so entertaining I have to recommend this show and I really hope to see a further evolution of flush in the future for something completely different is the butterfly who flew into the rave which just these three people dancing to rave music for an hour that is it that is the concept the music throughout the show evolves to different types of electronic music and really this is a presentation of endurance as they do not stop dancing throughout but the level of dance that they are presenting the lighting effects of the show and also the way that the music itself takes you on this journey of rave culture made this a fascinating our watch it's not going to be for everyone but it is it is one of the most unique options at fringe and if you want unique I cannot recommend this enough and my final four star show is a Beautiful Future is coming which is these three couples throughout history one from the past one from the present and one from the future all of them are dealing with climate change to some level I wish the level of performances was equally strong unfortunately I found myself drawn to certain couples more than others I wish that the way in which all of these three timelines had tied together just a little bit stronger but aspects of this story were incredibly compelling and climate change really the theme of the fringe this year and moving on to my four five star recommendations for part two of the fringe starting with another climate change story Hot Mess which is one of my favourite musicals I saw at fringe it is the only show I saw twice Hot Mess is the newest musical by Jack Godfrey and Ellie coote who also joined forces on 42 balloons that I saw in Chicago earlier this year Hot Mess is all about the toxic relationship between earth and humanity and it is so incredibly creative and fun and some of the best songwriting you will see at the fringe this year also one of the strongest cast Led by Tobias Turley and Danielle Steers who are incredible I need a cast album for this show immediately and fortunately I think we're getting it next week at least a limited EP this was one of my most anticipated shows of the fringe and it absolutely did not disappoint unfortunately I think it's sold out but if you are at fringe and you don't have tickets keep an eye out for returns and if you're in London they are doing a London production of this in the fall so definitely go see it if you can another one of my most anticipated hated shows that did not disappoint is Orpheus by wright and Grainger I love wright and grainger Half Man Half Bull was one of my favourite shows of last year's fringe Orpheus is a modern retelling of of course Orpheus and Eurydice about a musician Dave falling in love with Eurydice and like other works of wright and Grainger it is told through a variety of genres like folk music spoken word there's a little Bruce Springsteen in there and then incorporates the audience in this beautiful hour of storytelling I would definitely put this on par with Half Man Half Bull part 1 it didn't quite hit as hard for me as part 2 but I absolutely love this and cannot recommend it enough one of the biggest surprises of fringe is whole by American Sing Song which is this hilarious science fiction musical it's about this cult of religious fundamentalist who believe that the world is going to end and the only way to survive is to stick butt plugs up their a- it just escalates from there it sounds weird it is weird but it absolutely commits to the bit and does so so creatively brilliantly the entire thing is told by just two performers who are also performing their own music and sound effects it is one of the most bizarre shows I've seen at fringe but one that works so incredibly well aspects of the show are incredibly explicit so like don't bring kids but if you're an adult I cannot recommend this show enough and finally my final 5 star show is and then the Rodeo burned down which is again another xhloe and Natasha show after seeing all three of the shows that they have brought to fringe this is absolutely my favourite all of xhloe and Natasha's shows are full of clowning and absurdism but at the core is a very like central theme I feel like uh and then the Rodeo burned down is the most accessible of their works where it's very clear what the show is going for by the end of it but it is an incredible story about a Rodeo clown who wants to be a cowboy that ends up being a metaphor for something much larger Xhloe and Natasha's ability to perform with each other their timing their physicality and the way that they are able to weave in very clear themes into these absolutely absurdist narratives is unmatched again if you have a chance to see any of their shows I cannot recommend it enough they are such compelling performers and I cannot wait to see what they do next and those are my part 2 recommendations if you have anything that you've seen that you've loved drop it in the comments I am no longer in Edinburgh I'm filming this from Amsterdam but I may I may be going back so let me know what I should see if I decide to take a second trip
